summary.plain: In 1987 the ARGUS experiment at DESY's DORIS ring made the first observation of B-meson mixing: a neutral B meson can turn into its antiparticle. The effect is closely linked to the matter-antimatter asymmetry (CP violation) in the universe.
summary.technical: ARGUS (DORIS II, Υ(4S) region), 'Observation of B⁰-B̄⁰ mixing', Phys. Lett. B 192 (1987) 245-252: the first observation of neutral B-meson oscillation, a process closely linked to CP violation.

title: Observation of B0-B0 mixing
why_it_matters: Ziemann's history of German accelerators calls it the first observation of B-B̄ mixing, a process closely linked to the prevalence of matter over antimatter in our universe that is referred to as CP-violation.
